variants.name: "Analyzed sequencing data" must find analysis samples
variants._why: The base asserted entity_sampletype_codes contains D.SEQ. The system did exactly that — searched sampletype D.SEQ with keyword 'analyzed' — and returned ZERO records, then suggested trying A.SEQ itself. The corpus was enforcing the wrong mapping: analysed sequencing output lives in A.* analysis sample types (A.GEX, A.ALN, A.VCF, A.CNV, A.SCXP, A.CHRM).

turns.query: Show me analyzed sequencing data

variants.name: NHP samples from study GBM — ground truth is ZERO
variants._why: GBM does not exist at any level; all 408 NHP samples are in Impact. Turn 819 answered '89 NHP samples in GBM' — fabricated by hand-counting NHP- rows out of the unfiltered graph dump (its own batch histogram reports 4 for NHP-220416FLY-* where the graph has 8, and misses the largest batches). The old regex accepted 'could not' and 'no samples matched', so a total failure passed; it also accepted any confident number. Require an honest negative AND reject a confident non-zero sample count.

family_floor._note: Minimum OUTCOME assertion per family, applied by corpus.merged() to the LAST TURN of every variant in a listed family. Of 381 merged variants, 108 assert plan shape only and 194 assert only plumbing (api_ok / neo4j_ok, which say a request COMPLETED, not that it returned anything) — 79% cannot detect a wrong answer. Hand-editing 300 variants is not viable, so the floor is applied structurally.
family_floor._rules: A floor criterion is added only when the last turn does not already assert that FIELD, so a deliberate bound (e.g. row_count lte 20000) is never overwritten and never contradicted. Families not listed here get no floor. Tag a variant `no_floor` to opt out entirely — required wherever ZERO is the correct answer.
